programme: No coherent module. The twelve concordant factors span at least five unrelated embryonic developmental programmes read off their own target sets: cardiac specification (HAND1, NKX2-5 — MYH7, GATA4, PITX2, NPPB, DBH, TH), axial/limb patterning (HOXD13, HOXA10, HOXB7 — BMP2/4, IGFBP1, EPHA3/4/7, FGF2), neural-crest/epidermal specification (TFAP2A, TFAP2C, FOXD3 — ESR1, KRT10/14, MITF, NANOG), endoderm/hormone-gland specification (FOXA1 — AFP, GCG, SFTPB, TFF1), and a retinal/sensory-neuron factor (POU4F2) plus one general stress-response AP-1 factor (JUN). These target sets do not converge on a single pathway; they read as separate organ-fate programmes that happen to co-recur across patient subgroups rather than as one regulatory complex.
role_in_a: Not established — none of these factors beyond JUN has a documented role in fibromyalgia, and JUN's role (microglial polarization in nociplastic pain) is a single-factor association, not evidence for a shared module.
role_in_b: Not established as a joint programme — FOXA1 has isolated placements in MS-model Treg differentiation and IFN-beta/PI3K-Akt signalling, and JUN has a general neurodegeneration review, but neither co-occurs with the other ten factors in any retrieved source.
shared_axis: No defensible shared axis can be written from this list: the factors reflect distinct organ-specification programmes (cardiac, limb/axial, neural-crest, endodermal, retinal) with no retrieved evidence that any of them are co-regulated or co-expressed together in either blood immune cells or brain tissue.
reasoning: The eleven of twelve factors other than JUN and FOXA1 have no disease association in Open Targets and no on-topic literature for either disease, and even JUN/FOXA1 each have only isolated single-factor mentions that do not connect to one another or to the rest of the list. Treating a hand-picked developmental grab-bag (cardiac + limb + neural-crest + endodermal + retinal TFs) as a mechanism would be constructing a story the data do not support, so incoherent is the honest call.
support: PMID 38117896 — shows FoxA1+ regulatory T cell differentiation/metabolism relevant to an MS model, a single-factor finding not connected to the other eleven factors; PMID 28436428 — shows neuronal IFN-beta/PI3K-Akt-FoxA1 signalling in an MS model context, again isolated to FOXA1 alone; PMID 37069462 — discusses microglial polarization in fibromyalgia/nociplastic pain without naming JUN's co-factors here; PMID 41858835 — reviews c-Jun in neurodegeneration broadly, not specific to MS mechanism shared with the other factors.
how_to_falsify: Take ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq from matched fibromyalgia blood immune cells and MS brain/CSF-infiltrating cells and test whether FOXA1 and JUN (the only two factors with any disease placement) co-occupy shared regulatory elements near a common target such as IL6, and whether their target genes are co-expressed across independent cohorts beyond the 3 available here; independent co-occupancy and correlated expression across cohorts would overturn the incoherent call, while its absence would confirm it.
caveats: Blood (fibromyalgia) vs brain (MS) is a cross-tissue comparison built from only 3 independent cohort pairs underlying the 104 patient-group comparisons, so the high per-factor recurrence counts likely reflect correlated subgroups within few cohorts rather than fully independent replications. The tissue-generic exclusion list is informative here: it removed RELB, EBF1, FOXO3, RORA, MEF2C, NKX2-1, AR, KLF6, SOX9, ID3, HES6, NR5A2 — factors with substantially more plausible immune (NF-kB/RELB, Treg/FOXO3, Th17/RORA, B-cell/EBF1) or neural (MEF2C, NKX2-1) relevance to these two diseases than anything that survived. Their removal as 'generic to these tissues' means the more disease-relevant regulators were filtered out, leaving a residual list of idiosyncratic developmental patterning factors that do not cohere into a disease mechanism — this is the expected shape of a null result, not an oversight.
